title: Mara and the Thorn
premise: Freya Hartwell, a bone-carver who hears the dead through the relics she carves, has lived her whole life in Thornmere, a valley where magic cannot cross its borders. When a mute child arrives speaking a language older than any kingdom, Freya learns the child is a vessel carrying the voice of King Aldric—whose crown was bound to a devouring spirit called the Thorn a generation ago. The child's arrival means the binding is failing, and the Thorn will consume the king and spread beyond the valley within one turning of the moon. Freya must leave the only safe place she knows, guided by the dead and hunted by the king's justiciars who serve the Thorn unknowingly, to reach the capital and unbind Aldric before the coronation of his heir seals the Thorn's power permanently. In the end, Freya discovers that unbinding requires a willing vessel: the child offers itself, but Freya instead carves her own bones into the binding, trading her gift of hearing the dead for the silence of an ordinary life—while the freed king, remembering nothing, owes a debt to a carver he cannot name.
about_author: Beatrix Kavanagh is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing medieval legal documents before turning to fiction. She writes fantasy about ordinary craftspeople caught in the machinery of power, drawing on folklore of the English borderlands.

chapters.title: The Valley That Forgets
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Establishes daily life in Thornmere: carving bones for grieving families, hearing the dead's last words, hiding her gift from neighbors who fear magic. The emotional beat is quiet loneliness disguised as contentment—the reader feels how carefully Freya has built invisibility.

chapters.title: A Knock at Dusk
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. A mud-caked child appears at Freya's door during a storm, speaking a language no living person should know—and the bones in Freya's workshop begin answering in the same tongue. Emotional beat: dread mixed with reluctant tenderness as Freya takes the child in.

chapters.title: What the Bones Remember
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Through carved relics, a dead priestess explains the child carries King Aldric's true voice, exiled when the Thorn took his crown. The binding fails at the heir's coronation. Beat: Freya realizes the valley's safety is an illusion; the child is already dying.

chapters.title: The Justiciar's Road
chapters.summary: POV shifts to Ser Dain Voss, a royal justiciar tracking rumors of 'a witch and a changeling' toward Thornmere. Dain is honorable and loyal, believing he serves justice. Beat: dramatic irony—the reader sees his virtue being weaponized by the Thorn.

chapters.title: Leaving Thornmere
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Freya crosses the valley border for the first time; magic floods back into her senses painfully, and the dead of the wider world are louder, angrier, more numerous. Beat: disorientation and grief—she understands now what she traded away by staying hidden.

chapters.title: The Toll of Names
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. On the road, Freya learns the child's name—Wren—and that speaking it aloud lets Wren surface briefly from the ancient language. First real bond forms. Beat: warmth amid danger; Freya stops thinking of Wren as a burden.

chapters.title: Ash Market
chapters.summary: Dual POV (Freya/Dain). In a border town, Freya seeks a relic-map while Dain closes in; they nearly meet in a market square where the Thorn's influence has made people cruelly obedient. Beat: rising tension; Freya sees the Thorn's corruption firsthand for the first time.

chapters.title: The Dead Do Not Lie
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. A murdered informant's bones reveal that Dain once spared a village the crown ordered burned—proof not everyone serving the Thorn is lost. Beat: moral complication; Freya begins questioning whether justice lies outside the law entirely.

chapters.title: Hunted Through the Fens
chapters.summary: Dain's POV. Dain captures Freya's trail but hesitates when Wren speaks a single word in his dead sister's voice. Beat: doubt cracks Dain's loyalty; he falsifies his report for the first time, choosing mercy over orders.

chapters.title: The Convent of Quiet Sisters
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Refuge with an order of women who have been secretly preserving anti-Thorn lore for generations. Their abbess reveals the original binding ritual—and its terrible cost. Beat: hope shadowed by dread as Freya learns what unbinding demands.

chapters.title: Coronation Eve
chapters.summary: Dain's POV in the capital. Palace intrigue: the heir, Prince Corin, is cold and wrong-eyed; courtiers move like puppets. Dain witnesses the Thorn feeding openly. Beat: horror and disillusionment—Dain's faith in the crown collapses.

chapters.title: The Price of Silence
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. The abbess dies protecting them from justiciar raiders; her final words through her own skull-bone tell Freya the ritual needs a willing vessel of living bone. Beat: grief hardening into resolve; Freya suspects what the cost truly means.

chapters.title: Wren Speaks
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Wren surfaces fully and reveals the truth: the child volunteered generations ago, a bloodline of vessels bred for this moment, and Wren expects to die in the ritual. Beat: heartbreak—Freya refuses to accept a child's sacrifice as justice.

chapters.title: An Unlikely Alliance
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Dain finds Freya—not to arrest her, but to beg her help; he brings palace maps and the guard rotations. Uneasy trust forms between hunter and quarry. Beat: cautious alliance; loyalty redefined as something chosen, not commanded.

chapters.title: Beneath the Crown
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Infiltration via the catacombs beneath the palace, guided by the bones of kings buried there. They find Aldric alive but hollowed, barely a man. Beat: pity and fury—Freya hears the king's true self screaming inside his own body.

chapters.title: The Thorn Unmasked
chapters.summary: Dain's POV. The party is betrayed by a convent survivor turned informer; the Thorn manifests through Prince Corin, revealing it engineered the entire succession. Battle in the throne room's antechamber. Beat: climax begins—desperate, costly fighting.

chapters.title: What Loyalty Costs
chapters.summary: Dain's POV. Dain holds the antechamber door against corrupted guardsmen so Freya can reach the binding-stone, taking mortal wounds. His death buys minutes. Beat: tragic sacrifice—loyalty fulfilled at last, on his own terms, outside the law he served.

chapters.title: The Binding-Stone
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. At the stone, Wren moves to give itself—but Freya strikes first, carving the ritual into her own forearm bone with her carver's knife, offering her gift as the vessel. Beat: climax peak—self-sacrifice chosen over the easy acceptance of a child's death.

chapters.title: Unbinding
chapters.summary: Freya's POV, fragmented and dreamlike. Inside the ritual, Freya confronts the Thorn directly, hearing every soul it ever consumed, and uses their accumulated voices to tear it loose from crown and king. Beat: transcendent struggle—the dead become her army.

chapters.title: Aftermath of a Miracle
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The Thorn is destroyed; Aldric wakes whole but remembers nothing of his captivity or his rescuers. Wren survives, freed from the ancient tongue, an ordinary child. Beat: bittersweet victory—justice done, credit impossible.

chapters.title: The Silent Carver
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Freya returns to Thornmere with Wren, her gift gone—bones are only bones now, the dead silent at last. She grieves the loss and discovers an unexpected peace in it. Beat: quiet resolution; identity rebuilt without the thing that defined her.

chapters.title: A Debt Unnamed
chapters.summary: Final chapter, dual POV epilogue. King Aldric, haunted by a faceless memory, quietly repeals the witch-laws and sends a nameless pension to a carver in a forgotten valley. Freya burns the letter unread—or almost unread. Beat: closure with an open door; justice outside the law endures.
